title: The Ugly Duckling

full_text:
It was so glorious out in the country! The summer sun shone brightly on the golden wheat and green oats; storks walked on long red legs, chattering in Egyptian, while water-lilies floated on the quiet canals.

Under the broad leaves of a burdock plant, a mother duck sat upon her nest waiting for her eggs to hatch. Crack! Crack! One after another, the eggshells burst open, and tiny yellow ducklings poked out their heads, crying: "Cheep, cheep!"

Only one enormous egg remained unhatched. An old duck visited: "That is a turkey's egg! Leave it alone, you will never teach it to swim!" But the mother duck sat patiently until at last, the giant shell cracked. Out tumbled a large, awkward, grayish fledgling, looking clumsy and strange.

"What an ugly, overgrown creature!" cried the ducks in the yard. When they led the brood to the pond, the strange gray bird swam with effortless grace, using his legs better than any other. Yet in the poultry yard, the turkeys pecked him, the hens bit his neck, and the servant girl kicked him away with her shoe. Even his own brothers and sisters hissed: "If only the cat would catch you, you hideous fright!"

Heartbroken, the poor duckling flew over the hedge and fled into the wide moor where wild ducks lived. Through the bitter autumn, hunters' guns echoed through the reeds, dogs leaped through the water, and the terrified duckling hid in the rushes. He fled to a peasant's cottage where an arrogant cat and a haughty hen mocked him because he could neither purr nor lay eggs.

Winter arrived with piercing frost. The pond froze thicker and thicker; the duckling was forced to paddle with all his strength to keep a small breathing hole open in the ice, until at last he grew exhausted, froze fast in the ice, and lay stiff as stone. A farmer broke the ice with his wooden clog, carried him home, and revived him by the kitchen stove.

When spring returned, golden warmth filled the earth. The larks sang, and the apple trees blossomed. The duckling flapped his wings; they beat the air with tremendous power and lifted him high above the green meadows into a magnificent royal garden.

There, gliding upon the mirror surface of a clear lake, swam three dazzling, majestic white swans with curved necks and snow-white plumage.

"I will fly to these royal birds," thought the lonely duckling. "They will surely peck me to death because I am so ugly, but it is better to be killed by them than to be bitten by ducks, pecked by hens, and starved by winter!"

He flew down to the water and swam toward the magnificent swans with bowed head, whispering: "Kill me!"

He looked down into the clear crystal water. What did he see reflected in the mirror below?

He was no longer a clumsy, dark gray, hideous duckling! He was a swan—a glorious, graceful, radiant white swan!

The other swans swam around him, stroking his feathers with their beaks in joyous welcome. Little children ran into the garden, tossing bread and sweet cake into the water, shouting with clapping hands: "Look! There is a new swan! And he is the fairest and most magnificent of all!"

He rustled his feathers, lifted his slender neck toward the blue sky, and whispered from the depths of his overflowing heart: "I never dreamed of such happiness when I was the despised ugly duckling!"
moral: It does not matter having been born in a duck-yard, if only one has lain in a swan's egg; patience reveals true beauty.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Ugly Duckling"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.

discussion_questions.prompt: What is the main situation at the beginning of "The Ugly Duckling"?

How could you use this lesson in your own school or family life?

Imagine an alternate peaceful ending or a new creative adventure for these characters.
